full_judgment:
2. The short fact material for disposal of this petition is that the petitioner took loan from respondent No. 1, namely, the United Commercial Bank Ltd. The petitioner having failed to repay the loan respondent No. 1 filed Mortgage (Money) Suit No. 30 of 1992 in the Court of Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Mymensingh for foreclosure of the mortgaged money claiming a decree of Tk. 25,01,860. 24 paisa. The petitioner contested the suit by filing a written statement. But at the time of hearing he did not appear. Consequently, the suit was decreed ex parte on 23.6.92. Thereafter this leave petition has been filed stating that sections 6 and 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990(Act IV of 1990) are ultravires of the Constitution as it offence Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution. 

 5. A reference to Section 6(2) of Artha Rin Adalat shows that for filing any application for setting aside an ex parte decree under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure an applicant shall have to deposit 50% of the decretal amount. According to the learned Advocate this provision is violative of Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution. The learned Advocate in fact could not show as to how Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution are relevant in this case other than arguing that the law is very harsh for which if a decree is passed against a person he cannot prefer any appeal as it is difficult for him to deposit 50% of the decretal amount. We agree with the learned Advocate that the law is harsh but on that score we cannot knock down the provision 6(2) of the Act. The legislature while creating the forum of appeal under the Special Act has imposed some conditions and any one desirous of preferring an appeal must follow the procedure prescribed by law. Appeal under this Special Act is provided by this statute and this provision will guide the procedure of filing the appeal. The persons who are taking loan from the bank are a class apart and they are all treated equally under the law in force. We do not Lind that Section 6(2) of the Act is in any way violative of Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution. In the case of Zahirul Islam Vs. National Bank Limited and others, 46 DLR (AD) 191, this Division held while considering the maintainability of the writ petition observed as follows:- 

 "Section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 provides for appeal to the High Court Division within 30 days from the date of the decree on depositing at least half of the decretal amount, the appeal being non-entertain able without making such deposit. The petitioner without filing any appeal filed an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, namely, Writ Petition. No. 892 of 1991 which was dismissed summarily by a Division Bench of the High Court Division on 30. 6. 91 on the ground that the petitioner has an alternative and efficacious remedy by way of appeal"
